decisions.quote: Our first hypothesis was to replicate Feldman's (2009) model that established the developmental pathway of physiological regulation before age 1 → emotion regulation before age 1 → attention regulation between age 1-2 → self-regulation at age 5. In contrast, our study identified three major pathways: attention regulation at 6 months predicted physiological regulation at 15 months, attention regulation at 15 months predicted emotion regulation at 24 months, and attention regulation at 24 months predicted better self-regulation (greater executive functions, compliance, and fewer behavioral problems) in preschool age. Our findings are consistent with Feldman's (2009) study in several ways. First, both the current study and Feldman's (2009) study support the conceptualization that the development of self-regulation is an ongoing process during early childhood.
decisions.location: Discussion, Replication of Feldman's (2009) Model of Self-Regulation (line 61)
decisions.reason: Although the authors open the discussion by noting that their study replicated Feldman (2009) and provided favorable evidence for the integrative model, they explicitly contrast their empirical developmental pathways and continuous development findings with Feldman's unidirectional stagewise pathway while confirming other aspects (such as attention regulation predicting preschool self-regulation), making the replication outcome mixed.
